items.title: US business activity growth eases further in November, survey shows By Reuters
items.excerpt: Nov 23 (Reuters) - US business activity growth slowed further in November as high prices held back new orders and capacity constraints restrained output, but overall activity remains resilient, suggesting economic growth is continuing at an above-trend rate, a survey showed on Monday. S&P Global said its flash US Composite PMI Output Index, tracking the manufacturing and services sectors, eased to a four-month low of 54.6 this month from a final reading of 55.9 in October. A reading above 50 indicates expansion in the private sector. The pace of growth slackened in both manufacturing and the vast services sector, which is responsible for roughly two-thirds of US economic activity. The manufacturing PMI slipped to a three-month low of 54.5 from 54.9 in October, while the services PMI dropped to a four-month low of 54.7 from 56.1 last month. New business in services slid, while new orders in manufacturing were little changed. Input cost pressures eased but remain elevated and suggest inflation overall will stay well above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target. "Although output growth slowed in November, recent readings have been impressively strong, and the PMI surveys still point to GDP (gross domestic product) rising at an annualized rate of about 3% in the fourth quarter," said Chris Williamson, chief business economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence. "Growth also remained encouragingly broad-based across both manufacturing and services, with both sectors also still taking on additional staff in numbers that are indicative of a further strong payroll gain during November." The US economy grew at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter thanks to ongoing strength in consumer spending and the frenetic artificial intelligence build-out, and employers added a greater-than-expected 165,000 workers to their payrolls in October. "A key concern is the elevated cost of living and resulting pressures on affordability, and the survey price gauges remain at levels consistent with inflation running well above the Fed’s 2% target in the coming months, despite some moderation of the rate of inflation in November," Williamson said. "Supply disruptions, widely linked to global shipping delays, also appear to have become more widespread, adding to firms’ concerns about being able to fulfill orders and likely to add further to underlying price pressures in the coming months." The November 12-20 survey period also dovetailed with a sharp selloff in the US stock market, which has been a key pillar supporting consumer spending, on concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom. It was not clear from the survey data whether that development contributed to the softening in this month’s PMI readings.

The Medicaid work requirements, established under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) of 2025, are scheduled to take effect Jan. 1, 2027. CMS' new guidance gives states the option, if they submit a plan for CMS approval, to have until July 1, 2027, to fully implement them. They generally require affected beneficiaries to complete at least 80 hours of work, community service, or other qualifying activities each month, enroll in school at least half-time, or qualify for an exemption. During the optional extended period running from Jan. 1 through June 30, states may temporarily suspend Medicaid coverage denials and terminations for individuals who fail to demonstrate compliance with the work requirements. States must still assess whether applicants and beneficiaries meet the requirements or qualify for exemptions beginning Jan. 1. items.title: Alaska ends deal to give voter records to US Justice Department | US Midterm Elections 2026 News | Al Jazeera
items.excerpt: Published On 25 Nov 2026 25 Nov 2026 Alaska has terminated a memorandum of understanding that granted the United States Department of Justice (DOJ) access to the state’s voter rolls. On Monday, outgoing Lieutenant Governor Nancy Dahlstrom, who oversees the state’s elections, announced she had notified the Justice Department that Alaska was withdrawing from the 2025 memo, effective immediately. In a statement, Dahlstrom said her state had entered the agreement “in good faith to cooperate with our federal law enforcement partners”. But she acknowledged a shift had taken place after the 2026 midterm elections. “The circumstances have now changed,” Dahlstrom wrote. “The election has concluded and the agreement no longer serves a continuing purpose.” The reversal comes after months of pressure from the administration of President Donald Trump for states to surrender their voter rolls to federal authorities. Trump has argued that such information was necessary to root out fraud during the November 3 midterms. But officials in certain states argued that the federal government was encroaching on their constitutional authority. Under the US Constitution, only states have the power to administer elections. Experts have also called Trump’s claims of “rigged” elections unsubstantiated. ## No voters flagged for removal The memorandum, signed last December at the Justice Department’s behest, established terms under which federal officials could flag potentially ineligible voters on Alaska’s voter rolls. “Since that time, the DOJ has not identiﬁed any potentially ineligible voters or raised concerns regarding Alaska’s voter registration records,” the state Division of Elections said. “No voters were removed from Alaska’s voter rolls as a result of the agreement.”

items.title: Poll finds US voters want government to end Iran war regardless of terms | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
items.excerpt: Published On 25 Nov 2026 25 Nov 2026 A new poll has found that a majority of voters in the United States want an end to the US-Israel war on Iran immediately, even if it means accepting less favourable conditions. Overall, 55 percent of those surveyed agreed with an “end to the war now, regardless of the terms”. That number was even higher among Democrats and independents, who agreed with the statement at a rate of 80 percent and 59 percent, respectively. About 25 percent of Republicans said the same. A majority of Democratic voters also supported steps to pressure the administration of President Donald Trump to stop the conflict. Fifty-three percent of party members said they would favour Congress withholding funding for military operations, and 51 percent would back an “an Iran war-funding cutoff” in upcoming budget negotiations, even if the manoeuvre risked a government shutdown. The numbers were published on Tuesday as part of the latest Critical Issues Poll, released by the University of Maryland and the research firm Ipsos. Shibley Telhami, the poll’s principal investigator, said he was surprised by the level of support for ending the war, regardless of the terms. “We knew that people were strongly opposed to this war and wanted it to end,” he told Al Jazeera in a phone call. “What we were less sure of is what they would be willing to accept to achieve this.” The survey asked 1,022 US adults about their perspectives on the war. In one question, they were tasked with assessing with three options: whether to end the conflict immediately, escalate militarily, or continue on the current path in order to extract concessions from Iran. Just 21 percent of all respondents favoured the current path, and 18 percent supported escalation. “Clearly, the public mood is to end it now, whatever it takes,” said Telhami. ... Voters also appear sceptical about the US government’s arguments in favour of the war, which include dismantling Iran’s nuclear programme. The Critical Issues Poll found that only 28 percent of those surveyed believed that the war had left Iran in “worse position” to develop nuclear weapons. While the US has long voiced concerned that Iran could pursue nuclear arms, intelligence assessments have not found evidence that Tehran has authorised such a step since abandoning its nuclear weapons programme in 2003. The Strait of Hormuz has also emerged as a key issue, with Iran closing the waterway to commercial traffic early in the war. The Trump administration has responded with a naval blockade in the strait. Some 20 percent of the world’s oil supply passes through the maritime artery, and fuel prices have spiked as a result of the war. About 35 percent of respondents in Tuesday’s poll said that they believe Iran is now in control of the strait, while just 12.7 percent said the US is in control.
